svg.text: POWER & SMALL POWER LAYOUT — GROUND FLOOR
External / party wall cut by section, 300 mm —
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Reserved riser and the distribution route. Outlets,
circuits, board schedules and loads are the electrical
2. Coordination only. No fitting, outlet, diffuser, pipe or
cable is drawn, and no size, load or capacity appears.
Those are the services engineer's design; a layout
invented here would be thrown away, and in the meantime
3. What this sheet does fix is space: the riser reserved
through the building, the rooms that have to be served,
and the plant position. Those are expensive to change
later, which is why the architecture states them now.
4. The plan is run from the floor plan with its fittings
switched off, so it cannot drift from A-100 when a
5. Builder's work — holes, chases, upstands and bases — is to
be agreed against this layout before any slab is poured.
POWER & SMALL POWER LAYOUT — GROUND FLOOR
Coordination layout for the services engineer's design — no fitting, no size, no load. Not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P18 2026-10-07 scheme A adopted: serpentine balcony on every plan; site named
P19 2026-10-07 serpentine waist deepened 0.75 to 1.35 m; 15.7 m² of balcony a floor
P20 2026-10-07 internal partitions 100 mm red brick, specified by the client
P21 2026-10-07 300 mm external and party walls: brick, colour unrestricted
